items.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: I recorded his trio record you see? So you listen to Paul Carlon, it’s called “Tresillo.” And I’m on that and it’s just acoustic bass, tenor, and me on two congas only.

ctx.x: Yes he played here for an educational —

I recorded his trio record you see? So you listen to Paul Carlon, it’s called “Tresillo.” And I’m on that and it’s just acoustic bass, tenor, and me on two congas only. And you’re going to see how that works. Ask him about the new record. Tell him. So with that training, jazz things — because we go in and out, of different genres, different things, different colors, we can take it out and yet we have the tumbao in there you know, the main machine is running in there. So when I’m doing jazz I bring one conga and I…
I was imagining yesterday listening to the three of you what would cause you to look — give somebody a look like what are you doing. I mean you all knew each other.
